predecessors.name: Yuan dynasty
predecessors.text: Bozhou and Yingzhou in western Anhui, the Song base

successors.name: Zhu Yuanzhang's Wu
successors.text: Chuzhou and the Jiangnan province: Han Lin'er drowned in the Yangtze in January 1367 on the way to Nanjing and Zhu dropped the Song calendar

rulers.name: Han Lin'er
rulers.title: emperor of the Great Song (era name Longfeng)

ledger.x: 16 March 1355: Han Lin'er is proclaimed emperor of a restored Song at Bozhou.
May 1356: Han Lin'er names Zhu Yuanzhang head of Jiangnan Province.
June 1358: Liu Futong's army captures Kaifeng.
June 1358: the Song and the Yuan fight over Kaifeng and the Henan plain.
June 1358: the court moves to Kaifeng, the former Song capital.
1359: Chaghan Temur drives the Song back from the Bozhou-Yingzhou base to Anfeng.
September 1359: the fighting over Kaifeng ends with the Song withdrawal; the court then survived in Bozhou and later Anfeng.
1362 (bridging): the Song provinces other than Jiangnan are gone.
February 1363: Zhang Shicheng's general takes Anfeng and kills Liu Futong.
June 1363: the court is moved to Chuzhou, inside Zhu Yuanzhang's territory.
June 1363 (bridging): the Song court is housed at Chuzhou, a city of Zhu Yuanzhang's territory.
January 1367: the Song calendar is dropped.
January 1367: Han Lin'er drowns in the Yangtze and the Song ends.

wars.name: Red Turban northern expedition and the Kaifeng campaign
wars.outcome: The Song takes Kaifeng in June 1358 and moves its court there; Chaghan Temur retakes it in September 1359 and drives the court back to Bozhou and Anfeng.

wars.name: Siege of Anfeng
wars.outcome: Zhang Shicheng's troops, with Mongol forces, take Anfeng in February 1363 and kill Liu Futong; Zhu rescues Han Lin'er and moves the court to Chuzhou.

certainty.note: Every Song holding is a city district; the Kaifeng and Shandong holdings are described by name only.
